classification.INDEPENDENT: NOT SUPPORTABLE from the existing bytes: package-name difference is zero evidence (spec item 4); the two NYSE rule sets share a Quantopian ancestor and identically named inherited rules, and pandas_market_calendars additionally depends on and loads exchange_calendars at package level. Agreement between the emissions is a correlated consistency check, not independent verification of NYSE semantics.

common_ancestor_evidence: Both NYSE modules carry Quantopian, Inc. copyright headers (PMC calendars/nyse.py: 2016; EC exchange_calendar_xnys.py: 2018) — both packages' NYSE calendars descend from Quantopian/Zipline's original NYSE calendar code.

Identically named holiday rules appear in BOTH rule tables (e.g. USMartinLutherKingJrAfter1998, USWashingtonsBirthDay1964to1970, USPresidentsDay, MonTuesThursBeforeIndependenceDay, WednesdayBeforeIndependenceDayPost2013, USElectionDay1848to1967) — an inherited ancestral rule set.

The tables are nonetheless separate files with divergent, separately evolved entries (PMC: NYSE-suffixed splits such as USNewYearsDayNYSEpost1952/pre1952 and USJuneteenthAfter2022; EC: single USJuneteenth, BattleOfGettysburg, ChristmasBefore1954) and neither imports the other's tables; no runtime call-through exists on the PMC 'NYSE' native path.
Identical leading import pair in both NYSE modules (datetime.time; itertools.chain) is consistent with the shared lineage.
method: STATIC PASS ONLY: wheel bytes read as zip archive members; no install, no import, no execution of candidate code; no schedule generation

missing_authoritative_artifact.artifact: An immutable, hash-pinned capture of the NYSE's official published Holidays & Hours calendar (nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars), including its holiday and early-close listings for every year in the coverage interval [2024-09-16, coverage_end]; the NYSE-published closings document cited by the exchange_calendars source itself (nyse.com/pdfs/closings.pdf) is the exchange-published form of the same authority
missing_authoritative_artifact.authority: New York Stock Exchange (NYSE Group, Inc.) — the exchange itself
missing_authoritative_artifact.future_step: A separately authorized step fetches the NYSE-published calendar once, pins its SHA-256 in a committed capture receipt (source URL, retrieval timestamp, artifact hash), and the pinned implementation's sessions/holidays/early closes are then cross-checked date-by-date against that primary artifact; any disagreement = HOLD. No fetch was performed in this audit (network forbidden beyond spec/push).

path_B_pmc_key_XNYS_mirror.mechanism: mirror.py does `import exchange_calendars` at top level, reads exchange_calendars.calendar_utils._default_calendar_factories, and for EVERY factory key (including XNYS) dynamically creates a TradingCalendar subclass with _ec_class set to the exchange_calendars class; holidays/sessions/weekmask/offsets are delegated to the wrapped exchange_calendars instance via the .ec property
path_B_pmc_key_XNYS_mirror.warning: A pandas_market_calendars emission keyed 'XNYS' is the exchange_calendars XNYS calendar wrapped, not a second implementation. Any dual-emission design must pin the PMC key to 'NYSE' (native class) explicitly; keyed 'XNYS' it is one implementation observed twice.
